neet_phy_u19_t00_1.working: Arsenic is pentavalent (group 15). It acts as a donor and gives extra free electrons, so the semiconductor is n-type. B, Al and Ga are trivalent acceptors.

neet_phy_u19_t00_2.working: By the mass action law, p = ni^2/ND = (1.5e16)^2/4.5e22 = 2.25e32/4.5e22 = 5e9 m^-3.

neet_phy_u19_t00_3.working: sigma = n e mu = 1e22 x 1.6e-19 x 0.125 = 200 S/m, so rho = 1/200 = 5e-3 ohm m.

neet_phy_u19_t00_4.working: A is true: more carriers are thermally generated as temperature rises, so resistivity falls. R is true: electron mobility exceeds hole mobility. However, R does not explain the temperature dependence.

neet_phy_u19_t00_5.working: I is correct: donor atoms are neutral, so the crystal stays neutral while electrons are the majority carriers. II is correct: p ≈ NA and n = ni^2/NA, so doubling NA halves n.
